claims.claim: For any normal-state family E on separable H with finite relative-entropy Holevo capacity C, e(E)<=g_C(b2(E)) with the unchanged supplied finite modulus
claims.mechanism: Normal center from maximizing ensemble means; uniform spectral-tail control; normal finite compression; finite theorem and continuity

claims.claim: For any eta>0 a finite-outcome normal full-domain EB channel has error <=g_C(b2(E))+eta
claims.limits: Outcome count and rank depend on the experiment; no efficiency or uniform rank bound

claims.claim: The worst normal-target trace-distance error infimum over normal EB channels is attained, even for noncompact families
claims.mechanism: Pointwise sigma(T1,K) trace-nonincreasing EB subchannel; escaped-mass inequality; fixed normal trace filling
claims.limits: General optimizer may require continuous outcome representation; neither finite nor countable outcomes asserted

claims.claim: For relatively trace-compact E, the finite-outcome normal EB infimum equals the broad normal EB optimum
claims.mechanism: Uniform finite input/output compression of a fixed near-optimal normal EB map

claims.claim: Finite capacity and b2(E)=0 imply an exact normal countable projective EB fixer and exact normal classical broadcaster
claims.mechanism: Finite-outcome error-zero approximants force pairwise F=A and commutation; diagonalize through the normal center eigenspaces

claims.claim: Finite capacity and b=e=0 do not ensure any finite-outcome exact EB fixer
claims.example: sigma=diag(2^-n); rho_n=sigma+(2^-n/2)(P_n-P_1), n>=2; C<=ln(3/2); infinite linear span

claims.claim: Every finite-capacity normal-state family is relatively trace compact and has a normal reference sigma with D(rho||sigma)<=C

failed_routes.failure: Normal CPTP channels are not compact in pointwise trace norm; mass-escaping preparations have zero sigma(T1,K) limit. Unitality/normality cannot be assumed for arbitrary B(H) weak-star limits.
